statement: The 2026-09-07 ranking labels P0321 unsolved, but Lewin VI.B presents a qualitative KTHNY hexatic scenario rather than a single quantified theorem; its Theorem 47 covers translation invariance only for d=2,s>2 at finite inverse temperature.
assumptions: Dated ranking row; Lewin arXiv:2202.09240v2 Sections VI.A-B; no inference about 2026 openness.
source_quote: fast decay of translational correlations and slow decay of (six-fold) orientational correlations
proof_or_counterexample: Direct comparison of ranking title, VI.B paragraph, and Theorem 47 statement. The former leaves s and observables unspecified; Theorem 47 explicitly assumes s>d.
remaining_gap: Recover a fully quantified candidate theorem and perform definitive current-status check.
scope: source-text comparison only, not a mathematical solution

statement: For any finite simplicial triangulation of a closed orientable surface with every edge incident to two triangular faces, the degree charge q(v)=6-deg(v) obeys sum_v q(v)=6 chi. Thus the sum is zero on a torus; if degrees off 6 are only 5 and 7, their counts are equal.
assumptions: Closed triangulated surface, finite simplicial complex, no boundary, valid Euler characteristic chi; no Gibbs or Riesz assumption.
proof_or_counterexample: 3F=2E, sum deg=2E, V-E+F=chi imply E=3(V-chi) and hence sum(6-deg)=6V-2E=6chi.
remaining_gap: No bound on defect positions, densities, or thermodynamic Gibbs weights; verify torus-neighbor convention.
